name: Hereditary Paraganglioma-Pheochromocytoma Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Hereditary Paraganglioma-Pheochromocytoma Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of pathogenic germline mutation in SDHx genes (SDHA, SDHB, SDHC, SDHD, SDHAF2)
Diagnosis of paraganglioma or pheochromocytoma confirmed by histopathology or imaging
First-degree relative with paraganglioma or pheochromocytoma

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Pathogenic SDHx gene mutation plus presence of paraganglioma or pheochromocytoma tumor
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is essential for confirmation; family history supports diagnosis but is not mandatory.

pathognomonic.notes: Episodes of sudden high blood pressure due to catecholamine secretion
Severe headaches associated with tumor catecholamine release
Tumor detected by imaging or histology

common.notes: Drop in blood pressure upon standing

occasional.notes: Unintentional weight loss in some patients
Transient loss of consciousness or lightheadedness

rare.notes: Rarely caused by head and neck paragangliomas
Secondary erythrocytosis due to tumor secretion
Occasional symptom related to tumor location

laboratory: Elevated plasma and urinary catecholamines and metanephrines
imaging: MRI or CT showing paraganglioma or pheochromocytoma tumors
Functional imaging with 123I-MIBG scintigraphy or PET scans
genetic: Pathogenic germline mutations in SDHA, SDHB, SDHC, SDHD, or SDHAF2 genes

distinguishingFeatures: Typically solitary tumor without family history
Associated with retinal hemangioblastomas and renal cell carcinoma
Medullary thyroid carcinoma and hyperparathyroidism co-occurrence

redFlags: Sudden onset of severe hypertension with headache and sweating
Family history of paraganglioma or pheochromocytoma
Recurrent or multiple paragangliomas or pheochromocytomas
references: Lenders JWM, et al. Pheochromocytoma and Paraganglioma: An Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline. J Clin Endocrinol Metab. 2014.
Baysal BE. SDH mutations in tumorigenesis and inherited endocrine tumors. Trends Endocrinol Metab. 2002.
Neumann HP, et al. Germ-line mutations in nonsyndromic pheochromocytoma. N Engl J Med. 2002.
